validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently via four distinct origins that all describe this exact physical system -- Alaska DNR's own live CIGGS Pipeline database page, the Regulatory Commission of Alaska's 2014 CPCN consolidation docket (P-14-025), PHMSA's 2022 enforcement Final Order against Harvest Alaska for 'the CIGGS pipeline system', and Harvest Alaska LLC's own 2017 conversion application. Not a GEM-only entity. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of sibling Cook Inlet PIDs. The RCA's 2014 docket itself enumerates five separately-chartered pre-consolidation entities (KBPL, Beluga Pipeline Company, Kenai Kachemak Pipeline LLC/KKPL, Hilcorp Alaska d/b/a CIGGS, Hilcorp Alaska d/b/a Kenai Nikiski Pipeline/KNPL) that were merged only administratively into one CPCN/tariff (CPCN No. 668) under KBPL as of Nov 2014 -- CIGGS remained a physically and operationally distinct gathering/pipeline segment before and after that consolidation, so tracking it as its own GEM row alongside its former CPCN siblings appears correct (see cross_row_leads for the sibling-identification facts). CLASSIFICATION (PipelineType): 'transmission' is CORRECT despite the segment name 'Cook Inlet Gas Gathering System' -- PHMSA's 2022 Final Order explicitly applies 49 CFR Part 192 Subpart O (Gas TRANSMISSION Pipeline Integrity Management, citing 192.937(b) and 192.939(a)) directly against 'the CIGGS pipeline system', and the Anchorage Daily News (2015) covers it as a transmission line embroiled in an east-west Cook Inlet deliverability dispute among gas utilities. 'Gas Gathering System' is a legacy/historical company name, not evidence of a live gathering classification -- no change recommended to PipelineType.

cross_row_leads.facts: PHMSA's 2022 order describes a 'Beluga Transmission Pipeline' that is bi-directional: 'PSV X-028 is the primary overpressure protection for gas flows from the West CIGGS sources, and PSV-10056 is the primary overpressure protection for gas flow from the BRU [Beluga River Unit] Compressor... protects the Beluga Transmission Pipeline from overpressure... at Kaloa Junction.' Separately, the RCA's 2014 consolidation docket (https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=174074) names 'Beluga Pipeline Company (Beluga)' as one of the five original CPCN-holders (with KBPL, KKPL, CIGGS d/b/a name, and KNPL d/b/a name) 100%-owned by Hilcorp Alaska, LLC and folded administratively into KBPL's single CPCN No. 668 in Nov 2014, while remaining a physically distinct system tied into Kaloa Junction alongside CIGGS.

Harvest Midstream's own company history: 'In 2012... we acquired the Cook Inlet Pipeline, which gathers oil produced offshore, in addition to the Cook Inlet Gas Gathering System and the Kenai Nikiski Pipeline, which both transport natural gas' -- Kenai Nikiski Pipeline was acquired in the SAME 2012 transaction as CIGGS. The 2014 RCA consolidation docket (https://aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=174074) separately identifies 'Hilcorp Alaska, LLC d/b/a Kenai Nikiski Pipeline (KNPL)', 100%-owned by Hilcorp Alaska, LLC, one of the five entities folded into KBPL's consolidated CPCN 668.

Same Harvest history passage: 'Harvest acquired the Kenai Kachemak Pipeline, which transports natural gas on the Kenai Peninsula in Alaska' (2012, same era as the CIGGS/Kenai Nikiski acquisitions). The 2014 RCA docket names 'Kenai Kachemak Pipeline, LLC (KKPL)' as one of the five CPCN-holders (CPCN Nos. 448, 711, 668, 689 across the group) consolidated under KBPL, 100%-owned by Hilcorp Alaska, LLC.
